items.text: Sarah will document the meeting notes and store them in the shared folder for reference.
The selling price of the remote control is set at 25 euros.
The production cost is set at 12.50 euros.
The profit target is set at 50 million euros in the first year.
Team members are to draw their favorite animal on the whiteboard and describe its key characteristics.
Speaker S2 will describe their animal concept (a sitting dog) and its key features: supportive, loyal, and intuitive.
Speaker S3 will draw a crocodile and describe its characteristics as scary and strong.
Speaker S4 will draw an eagle and describe its characteristics as independent and free-spirited.
The team agrees that the product should be original, user-friendly, and appealing to a wide market including older adults and pets.
The product development process will follow three stages: functional design, conceptual design, and detailed design.
What is the equivalent of 25 euros in pounds?
Should the product price be undercut to compete with existing market products?
Explore the integration of an LCD display and menu-based navigation in remote controls, inspired by mobile phone design.
Investigate the feasibility of a dual-function remote control with basic buttons and a menu system featuring clear symbols and pictures for intuitive use.
Consider a flip-top remote control design to provide a larger screen when flipped open, potentially saving space and improving usability.
Evaluate the need for large print or accessibility features on the screen to support older users who may struggle with small text.
Assess whether the remote control design should prioritize simplicity and intuitiveness over fashion or premium materials.
Determine if the remote control should be accessible to older generations, including those who cannot program devices or understand complex interfaces.
The remote control should be designed to be usable by all age groups, including older users who may not be familiar with complex interfaces or programming.
The remote control should avoid excessive buttons and complex layouts, focusing instead on intuitive, self-explanatory design with clear symbols and basic functions.
The design should not require users to be technically proficient, such as programming or navigating menus, to operate the device.
The remote control should be accessible internationally, supporting use across different markets (e.g., Australia, America) without requiring language-specific adaptations.
The remote control should not need to be fashionable or use expensive materials like metal, but can instead use lightweight, moldable plastic for cost efficiency.
The remote control should avoid complex operating systems or confusing interfaces, such as those found in some modern smartphones, to prevent user confusion.
